newsitem.title: CUBA: Grenada moves to boost ties with Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Grenada moves to boost ties with Cuba.

text.p: Grenada's Prime Minister Keith Mitchell, turning a new page in relations with communist-ruled Cuba, said on Wednesday his country wanted to revitalise ties with Havana and benefit from Cuban expertise in health, agriculture, tourism and sports.

Mitchell, who signed a bilateral economic cooperation agreement with Cuban President Fidel Castro on Tuesday, said his country believed that stronger relations with Cuba would benefit both countries and the wider Caribbean community.

"We recognise that we have to use all friends, regardless of what ideological labels they have, to push our country forward," the Grenadian premier told a news conference after a four-day official visit to Cuba.

The visit and the cooperation accord showed that both countries wanted to put behind them the memory of the 1983 U.S. invasion of Grenada which ended four years of rule by a Cuban- and Soviet-backed leftist government. Twenty-four Cuban construction workers were killed during the U.S. invasion.

Mitchell made a point of praising the contribution made by Cuba to Grenada's economic and social development between 1979 and 1983, when the revolutionary New Jewel Movement was in power. He singled out Cuban help in health and education and in starting construction of an international airport.

"We believe that Cuba played an immense role in the development of our country, and gave us support that we are benefitting from today," he said. "We would therefore like to revitalise this positive relationship," he added.

Giving details of the cooperation areas agreed between both countries, Mitchell said Grenadian professionals would be able to receive health care training in Cuba. Cuba had also agreed to treat serious medical cases from Grenada and two seriously sick patients would be flown to Havana immediately for care.
Mitchell said Grenada would seek Cuban technical assistance to develop its agro-processing industry, for example for traditional export crops like nutmeg, cocoa and bananas.
In sports, Cuba would be able to assist in the construction of a national sports stadium by supplying cement and steel.
Mitchell stressed the potential of Cuba's fast-growing tourist industry and said Grenadians could also receive tourism training on the communist-ruled island.
"We want to use what Cuba has most -- the available technical and human resources," he said.
He explained the move to strengthen Cuban-Grenadian ties by underlining the need for Caribbean unity and economic integration in a world dominated by large economic blocs.
Grenada, part of the English-speaking Caribbean Community (Caricom), is currently chairman of the 25-member Association of Caribbean States (ACS), Cuba is also an ACS member.
